title: Oner
description: A oner shot is designed to play as if the scene were one take, with no visible edits. It may be a true single take or a stitched oner whose joins hide in whips, darkness, or crossing bodies.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Use it when geography, breath, and choreography should feel like one continuous push: a backstage spiral, a trench, an extraction through apartments. Hidden cuts are allowed only if they are invisible.
The audience should not be able to point to the splice. The camera and the blocking are one machine.
It is the wrong tool when the ethical claim is uncut duration, or when the scene is a quiet two-person talk that only needs a master. A true long take refuses the stitch.
A oner may use it. Do not call three coverage angles a oner because the editor was smooth.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Choreograph a path that can be performed, then decide where a join could hide if the take cannot be true. Steadicam, crane, and handheld all work if the breath stays consistent.
Match lighting and eyelines across stitches. Prompt: Apparent oner of [Subject], a whole scene as one take, hidden cuts allowed only if invisible.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the scene is a ride through connected actions, such as a backstage spiral or a trench crossing. Do not use it for a static conversation that only needs coverage.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Long Take emphasizes uncut duration as a fact. A oner emphasizes the ride and may be stitched.
Steadicam is often the support. An Invisible Cut is the join.
Tracking Shot and Follow Shot can exist inside a oner without making every track a oner.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Birdman plays backstage panic as one apparent breath, stitches hidden. 1917 connects trench and field into a continuous war path, also stitched.
Extraction runs apartment and vehicle action as a designed single-take sequence. Compare those with Russian Ark, a true feature-length take, if the claim is uncut fact rather than ride.

blocks.text: Write a whole scene as one take. Still: a frame from the path, not proof.
Video: A continuous oner following [Subject] through connected actions without a visible cut. Name rooms, turns, and the human anchor.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is ordinary coverage, or a Long Take you secretly cut. The tell is a change of breath, a jump in extra positions, or a whip that does not match.
Fix: one visible path, matched energy across any hidden join, and no insert that admits the splice.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Oner in film?
A oner is a shot designed to play without visible edits, whether it is a true single take or a stitched sequence whose joins do not read.
Oner vs Long Take
A long take is continuous recorded duration. A oner is the ride: it can be true or stitched, as long as the audience cannot see the cut.
When should I use Oner?
When the scene should feel like one breath through connected spaces and actions, and coverage would leak the charge.
How do I prompt Oner for AI image or video?
Write a continuous oner following [Subject] through connected actions with no visible cut. Name the path. Allow hidden cuts only if they stay invisible.
